markingScheme.criterion: Quotes at least two of the student's own logged Moth Island readings (a habitat and generation with its light and dark moth counts, e.g. clean forest generation 3: 14 light, 6 dark) as evidence.
markingScheme.accept: Any two genuine habitat/generation/count readings from the student's own Investigation Record rows; exact wording not required.
markingScheme.insufficient: A general claim ('there were more light moths') with no actual logged readings quoted.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains why the numbers changed: moths that blend in with the bark are harder for the bird to see so more of them survive, while the moths that stand out are eaten more.
markingScheme.accept: Any valid phrasing that the colour matching the bark gives camouflage so those moths survive better and the contrasting colour is spotted and eaten.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying only 'the birds ate them' or 'they changed' with no link to camouflage/colour matching the habitat.

markingScheme.criterion: States that the surviving moths breed and pass their colour to their offspring, so the proportion of that colour is higher in the next generation (and that the pattern reverses on the other bark colour).
markingScheme.accept: Any correct statement that survivors reproduce and inherit/pass on their colour so the population changes over generations; an explicit comparison of the two habitats earns it.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying only 'the moths changed colour' (individual moths do not change) or 'they got used to it'.

markingScheme.criterion: Identifies variation and survival: before spraying some insects already had a trait (a gene/mutation) that let them survive the insecticide, and when the field was sprayed those insects survived while most died.
markingScheme.accept: Any correct statement that resistant insects already existed (natural variation or an earlier mutation) and survived the spray.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying 'the insects got used to the spray' with no mention of some already being different.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains inheritance over generations: the survivors reproduced and passed the resistance trait to their offspring, so the proportion of resistant insects increased until almost all were resistant.
markingScheme.accept: Any valid reference to the survivors breeding and the resistance trait being inherited so it spreads over generations.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying 'they all became resistant' without breeding/passing on/generations.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains why Lamarck's idea does not fit: traits gained by trying or by use are not inherited, and the resistance existed (by variation or mutation) before the spraying rather than being created by the insects wanting it.
markingScheme.accept: Any correct statement that trying/stretching/effort does not change genes or get passed on, or that resistance was already present.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying only 'Lamarck was wrong' or 'it is a different theory' with no reason.
